summary: Monolith architecture: Next.js (React) frontend, Node.js (NestJS, TypeScript) backend, PostgreSQL database on Google Cloud (Cloud Run + Cloud SQL).

frontend.justification: SEO-critical pages need server-side rendering / pre-rendering; matches team language(s): javascript, typescript; well suited to marketplace. React with SSR/SSG; the most adopted React meta-framework. Strong SEO and ecosystem.

alternatives.why_not: Scored lower on this scenario's specific priorities and constraints.
Weaker server-side rendering for SEO-critical pages.
Weaker server-side rendering for SEO-critical pages.

tradeoffs: Tied to React ecosystem; Vercel-style hosting assumed for the smoothest path.

backend.justification: Matches team language(s): javascript, typescript; well suited to marketplace; strong realtime/WebSocket support. Structured TypeScript framework; first-class WebSocket support and a huge ecosystem.
tradeoffs: Single-threaded event loop; CPU-heavy work needs worker queues.

database.justification: Well suited to marketplace; fits a balanced workload. The default relational choice: JSONB, full-text search, strong integrity, huge ecosystem.

alternatives.why_not: Higher running cost for a cost-sensitive project.
Scored lower on this scenario's specific priorities and constraints.
Scored lower on this scenario's specific priorities and constraints.

tradeoffs: Vertical scaling first; very high write scale needs read replicas/partitioning.

hosting.justification: First-class support for the chosen framework(s). Cloud Run scales containers to zero; Mumbai/Delhi regions; full compliance coverage.

alternatives.why_not: Scored lower on this scenario's specific priorities and constraints.

tradeoffs: Cloud SQL costs at scale; some GCP services lag AWS in India regions.

supporting.justification: Built-in tsvector search; plenty for moderate datasets, no extra service to run.
WebSocket layer with rooms and fallbacks; you scale it yourself (Redis adapter).
UPI, cards and subscriptions for India; PCI scope stays with the PSP.
Managed auth with phone OTP and social providers; generous free tier.
In-memory cache for hot reads, sessions and rate limits.
Background jobs on top of Redis; no extra broker for Node teams.
Web frontend does not cover the required mobile platforms; Expo ships Android/iOS from one JavaScript/TypeScript codebase, reusing the backend API.
tradeoffs: Some native modules require ejecting from Expo.

supporting.justification: Free-tier CDN, caching, WAF and DDoS protection.
CI/CD next to the code; free tier covers small teams.
Error monitoring with a free tier; self-hostable if needed.

assumptions: Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote; real bills depend on traffic shape and discounts
